stories.title: Tracking down the 16-year-old WAL-reset SQLite bug
stories.blurb: Tailscale engineers hunted a corruption bug lurking in SQLite's Write-Ahead Logging for 16 years — and lived to tell the tale. A masterclass in low-level debugging, race conditions, and why you never assume the database is fine. Essential reading for anyone who ships SQLite in production.

stories.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813
stories.blurb: DeepSeek drops a fresh flagship model today, landing straight on OpenRouter for easy API access. The 373-comment thread is already full of benchmark comparisons and Claude/GPT-4o head-to-heads — if you're evaluating models for coding workflows, this one's worth a spin right now.

stories.title: AI is removing the middle class of software engineering?
stories.blurb: A provocative argument that AI coding tools are bifurcating the field — turbocharging senior engineers while eroding the entry-level ramp that used to build mid-career developers. 780 comments means this hit a nerve. Mandatory reading if you use Claude Code daily and wonder what you're automating away.

stories.title: Qwen3.8-2.4T
stories.blurb: Alibaba's Qwen team releases a massive 2.4-trillion-parameter MoE model — one of the largest openly-available weights yet. The active parameter count keeps inference tractable, making this a landmark for local and cloud AI deployments alike. Expect fast community fine-tunes to follow.

stories.title: License plate reader searches should require a warrant
stories.blurb: A criminologist makes the civil-liberties case against warrantless bulk ALPR queries, backed by data. As LPR networks quietly blanket every major city, this is the legal and technical argument your city council probably hasn't heard yet. The comment thread digs into Fourth Amendment doctrine and chilling effects.

stories.title: Delta
stories.blurb: Zed introduces Delta, a new agentic diff/review layer built into the editor. It's designed to let AI make and explain multi-file edits in a reviewable, stepwise way — directly addressing the 'AI vomited a wall of changes' problem. If you're living in an AI-assisted coding workflow, this is the UX evolution to watch.

stories.title: Grok 4.6
stories.blurb: xAI pushes another Grok iteration with claimed reasoning and coding improvements. The 487-comment thread is characteristically heated — benchmarks, skepticism, and comparisons to today's other model drops (DeepSeek V4 Pro, Qwen3). A busy Wednesday in the frontier model race.

stories.title: uBlock Origin Is Giving Up the Fight to Keep Ads Off Facebook
stories.blurb: uBlock Origin's maintainer waves the white flag on Facebook ad blocking — Meta's server-side ad injection has become technically unblockable without breaking the site. This is a significant moment for the browser privacy ecosystem and a preview of where the ad-blocker arms race is heading.

stories.title: Someone is running mass vulnerability scans, spoofing AI bots like ClaudeBot
stories.blurb: Researchers have caught large-scale vulnerability scanners masquerading as ClaudeBot and other legitimate AI crawlers to slip past bot-detection rules. A stark reminder that your robots.txt allowlist is now an attack surface — and that Claude's good name is being borrowed without permission.

stories.title: Why tiny JPEGs look different in Chrome
stories.blurb: A deep dive into why Chrome's JPEG rendering diverges from other browsers at small sizes — touching on color profiles, chroma subsampling, and the browser's image pipeline. If you've ever scratched your head at a photo looking subtly wrong on the web, here's the pixel-level explanation.

stories.title: HTML over WebSockets: real-time SPAs with barely any JavaScript
stories.blurb: A compelling walkthrough of server-driven UI via WebSocket HTML streaming — the HTMX/Phoenix LiveView pattern explained from first principles. For Angular devs curious whether there's a lighter path for certain real-time features, this is a thought-provoking counterpoint.

stories.title: High-Res Photo Shows Sand-Capped Butte Rising from Mars Plain of Polygons
stories.blurb: A jaw-dropping HiRISE image of an isolated mesa on Mars surrounded by cracked polygon terrain — the kind of shot that looks almost surreally painted. PetaPixel breaks down the photography and geology for a satisfying double read.

stories.title: Show HN: Woxi - Open-source Mathematica / Wolfram Language reimplementation
stories.blurb: Woxi is an ambitious open-source reimplementation of the Wolfram Language, aiming to break the Mathematica paywall for symbolic computation. Early days but already functional for core expressions — one to bookmark if you do any scientific or mathematical computing.

stories.title: ChatGPT Desktop (Codex Desktop) for Linux
stories.blurb: OpenAI quietly releases Codex Desktop for Linux, bringing the agentic coding assistant to the platform previously left out. Directly relevant if you evaluate AI coding tools across platforms — and a pressure signal for Claude Code's cross-platform roadmap.

stories.title: Mushroom behind 'tiny people' hallucinations identified
stories.blurb: Scientists have pinned down the specific fungal species responsible for Lilliputian hallucinations — a peculiar perceptual distortion where users see miniaturized people. The neuroscience of why this compound targets size perception specifically is genuinely fascinating.

stories.title: Lovable raises $400M Series C
stories.blurb: The AI-powered app builder Lovable closes a monster $400M round, cementing vibe-coding as a serious venture category. The valuation and growth numbers here tell you something about where non-developer app creation is heading — and what it means for professional devs who build the underlying tools.

stories.title: The hardest working font in Manhattan (2025)
stories.blurb: A love letter to Helvetica's ubiquity on New York City signage — beautifully photographed and typographically rigorous. A slow-scroll treat for anyone who cares about design, and a reminder that font choices outlast the designers who made them by decades.

stories.title: Why Target Common Lisp for Code Generation?
stories.blurb: A thoughtful argument that Common Lisp's homoiconicity and macro system make it an unusually good compilation target for LLM-generated code. Counterintuitive but well-reasoned — especially interesting if you think about AI code correctness and verifiability.

stories.title: Shade Map
stories.blurb: An interactive map that simulates sun and shadow for any location and time of day — useful for route planning, photography golden-hour scouting, or just figuring out which café patio stays shaded all afternoon. Instantly usable and unexpectedly delightful.

stories.title: 2026 Eclipse Webcams
stories.blurb: A community-curated dashboard of live webcam feeds for the 2026 solar eclipse — bookmark this now so you're not scrambling for a stream on the day. Cloud coverage maps are also aggregated, making it the one-stop shop for remote eclipse watching.
